docs.text: MIECO - Metabolite Identification Evidence Code Ontology Welcome to the MIECO documentation! MIECO is a DL ontology based on ECO to serve Metabolomics repositories with a formal ontology of terms describing evidences for molecule identification assertions. It was built in a middle-out approach, starting with a LC-MS Assay use case and then successively expanded to integrate other metabolomics techniques like NMR, UV, IR Spectrometry and others. Quick Links GitHub Repository Issue Tracker Documentation You can find descriptions of the standard ontology engineering workflows here .

docs.text: Continuous Integration This document describes the CI pipeline for MIECO. Overview MIECO uses GitHub Actions for continuous integration. The CI pipeline runs automatically on: - Every push to the master branch - Every pull request targeting the master branch Workflows QC Workflow ( .github/workflows/qc.yml ) Runs ontology quality control checks using the ODK Docker container: Reasoning test : Validates the ontology is consistent using the ELK reasoner SPARQL validation : Runs SPARQL queries to check for common errors ROBOT report : Generates a quality report The CI runs with: make test IMP=false PAT=false MIR=false The IMP=false , PAT=false , and MIR=false flags skip import refreshing, pattern processing, and mirror refreshing for faster CI runs. Docs Workflow ( .github/workflows/docs.yml ) Automatically rebuilds the MkDocs site and commits the generated HTML to docs/ on every push to master. GitHub Pages is then configured to serve from that docs/ folder — no separate gh-pages branch required. This is intentionally simpler than using a third-party action such as mhausenblas/mkdocs-deploy-gh-pages because: It has no external action dependency (the mhausenblas action is unpinned and could change or disappear). There is no gh-pages branch to manage — everything lives on master . GitHub Pages setup is a single repository setting: serve from /docs on master . The generated HTML is visible directly in the repository. Documentation can also be updated entirely without CI: run mkdocs build locally and commit the docs/ output. Viewing CI Results Check the Actions tab to see CI results. For more information, see: https://oboacademy.github.io/obook/howto/odk-workflows/

docs.text: Editors Workflow This document describes how to edit the MIECO ontology. Prerequisites Install Docker Clone the repository: git clone https://github.com/sneumann/MIECO Open a terminal and navigate to src/ontology Editing the Ontology The source file to edit is src/ontology/mieco-edit.owl . You can use Protégé to edit the ontology. Running Quality Checks After editing, run the quality checks locally using the ODK wrapper: cd src/ontology ./run.sh make test IMP=false PAT=false MIR=false Committing Changes After verifying your changes pass quality checks: git add src/ontology/mieco-edit.owl git commit -m "Brief description of change" git push origin master The CI pipeline will automatically run quality checks on your commits. For more information, see the ODK documentation .
docs.title: Editors Workflow

docs.text: Release Workflow This document describes how to make a release of MIECO. Prerequisites Install Docker Ensure all changes are committed and pushed to master Ensure the CI is passing Making a Release Navigate to src/ontology Run the release pipeline: cd src/ontology ./run.sh make prepare_release Review the generated release files in the repository root Commit the release files: git add mieco.owl mieco-base.owl git commit -m "Release YYYY-MM-DD" git push origin master Create a release tag on GitHub: Go to https://github.com/sneumann/MIECO/releases/new Tag: vYYYY-MM-DD Title: YYYY-MM-DD Click "Publish release" Release Artefacts The following release artefacts are generated: mieco.owl - The primary release file mieco-base.owl - The base release (no imported axioms) For more information, see the ODK release documentation .
docs.title: Release Workflow

docs.text: Manage your ODK Repository This document describes how to keep your ODK repository up-to-date. Updating the ODK From time to time, the ODK is updated with new features and bug fixes. To update your repository: Check the ODK CHANGELOG for updates Update the ODK version in src/ontology/mieco-odk.yaml if needed Run the repository update: cd src/ontology ./run.sh make update_repo Review the changes and commit them: git add -A git commit -m "Update ODK to vX.Y.Z" git push origin master ODK Version The current ODK version used in this repository is specified in: - .github/workflows/qc.yml (container image version) - src/ontology/Makefile ( ODK_VERSION_MAKEFILE variable) For more information, see: https://oboacademy.github.io/obook/howto/odk-update/
docs.title: Manage your ODK Repository

docs.text: Repository File Structure This document describes the file structure of the MIECO ODK repository. Directory Structure MIECO/ ├── .github/ │ └── workflows/ │ ├── qc.yml # CI quality control workflow │ └── docs.yml # Documentation build & commit workflow ├── docs/ # Generated HTML documentation (served by GitHub Pages) ├── docs_src/ # Documentation source files (Markdown, edit these) │ ├── index.md # Documentation home page │ └── odk-workflows/ # ODK workflow documentation ├── mkdocs.yaml # MkDocs configuration (docs_dir: docs_src, site_dir: docs) ├── ontology/ # Legacy ontology files (backward compatibility) │ ├── MIECO.owl # Original OWL file │ └── MIECO.obo # OBO format version ├── src/ │ └── ontology/ │ ├── mieco-edit.owl # Source ontology file (edit this!) │ ├── mieco-odk.yaml # ODK project configuration │ ├── Makefile # ODK Makefile (DO NOT EDIT) │ ├── mieco.Makefile # Custom Makefile overrides │ ├── run.sh # Docker wrapper script │ ├── catalog-v001.xml # OWL catalog for imports │ └── README-editors.md # Editor instructions └── README.md # Repository README Key Files src/ontology/mieco-edit.owl : This is the source file that editors should modify. src/ontology/run.sh : Use this to run make commands inside the ODK Docker container. src/ontology/Makefile : The main build file generated by ODK. Do not edit this directly. src/ontology/mieco.Makefile : Add custom make rules here. src/ontology/mieco-odk.yaml : ODK project configuration. Release Files After running make prepare_release , the following files are generated at the repository root: - mieco.owl - Primary release file - mieco-base.owl - Base release (without imported axioms)
docs.title: Your ODK Repository Overview

docs.text: Setting up Docker for ODK This document describes how to set up Docker for use with the ODK. Installation Install Docker Desktop for your platform: Mac Windows Linux Verify Docker is working: docker run hello-world Pulling the ODK Image Pull the ODK Docker image: docker pull obolibrary/odkfull:v1.5.4 Using run.sh The run.sh script in src/ontology/ wraps Docker commands for you: cd src/ontology ./run.sh make test For more information, see: https://oboacademy.github.io/obook/howto/odk-setup/
docs.title: Setting up Docker for ODK
